reason: Section 49 states the effect of adopting a rural community rural plan on commitments and inconsistent development.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural community rural plan effect on proposals and inconsistent development

evidenceText: does not commit the rural community or the Province

proposedGroups.reason: The section contrasts no commitment by the rural community or Province with the restraint on rural community development inconsistent with plan proposals or policies.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that adopting a rural community rural plan does not commit projects but prevents inconsistent rural community development.

reason: Section 50 is a single rural-community rural-plan review workflow with start, completion, and reporting duties.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural community rural plan ten-year review, completion deadline, and report

evidenceText: review is commenced of a rural plan at least once every ten years

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections connect the ten-year review trigger, 36-month completion deadline, and duty to provide the report to the Minister.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a rural community rural plan review must start, when it must conclude, and when the review report goes to the Minister.

reason: Section 51 is a coherent rural-district rural-plan regulation preparation rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister rural district regulation, preparation, studies, and certification

evidenceText: Within five years after the date a rural district is established

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections state the Minister's five-year regulation duty, preparation or amendment under planning direction, required studies and consultation, and certification.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how rural district rural plans are made by regulation and the preparation, study, consultation, and certification requirements.

reason: Section 51.1 is a coherent rule for Crown actors considering rural district rural plans and seeking approval for non-conforming construction.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown development conformity with rural district rural plans

evidenceText: shall consider the rural plan adopted for the rural district

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections cover consideration of the rural district rural plan, approval for listed non-conforming construction, and the relocation, removal, demolition, alteration, or repair exception.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how Crown actors must consider rural district rural plans and when Lieutenant-Governor in Council approval is required or unnecessary.

reason: Section 52 is a large rural-district regulation source with separate topics for area/powers, plan content, objections, fees and incorporated effects, and publication/validity rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural district regulation area designation and council-equivalent powers

evidenceText: shall designate an area for the purpose of the application of the regulation

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 52(1) requires area designation and allows the Minister to include things a council may do by by-law.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what the Minister must designate and may provide in a rural district regulation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural district regulation policies, zoning map, modified zoning rules, and policy priority

evidenceText: A regulation under this Division shall contain

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections list required policy statements, proposals, zoning provisions and map, apply zoning by-law rules with modifications, and give policy or proposal priority over zoning provisions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the required contents of a rural district regulation and how its policies or proposals relate to zoning provisions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Written objections and substantial amendments before rural district regulation

evidenceText: shall not make a regulation under this Division until after the 14 days

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require the Minister to wait for the 14-day objection period, consider written objections, and repeat notice procedures after substantial amendments.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the objection timing and substantial-amendment rules before a rural district regulation is made.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural district zoning fees, non-commitment, review, and incorporated rules

evidenceText: the fee shall be paid

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover zoning amendment fees, payment to the regional service commission, no provincial commitment to proposals, review, rural-plan effect, and section 125 rules.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the fee, non-commitment, review, and incorporated-effect rules for rural district regulations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations Act exclusion and Royal Gazette publication for rural district regulations

evidenceText: shall be published in The Royal Gazette

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections exclude the Regulations Act and require Royal Gazette publication while preserving validity despite failure to publish.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the publication rule for rural district regulations and why a failure to publish does not affect validity.

reason: Section 52.1 is a focused rural-district rural-plan review rule with a start and completion deadline.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural district rural plan ten-year review and completion deadline

evidenceText: shall ensure that a review of a rural plan for a rural district is commenced

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections require the Minister to commence a review at least every ten years after the regulation is made and conclude it within 36 months.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister must review a rural district rural plan and when that review must conclude.

reason: Section 53 is a large zoning by-law source whose educational topics divide by drafting requirements, zoning powers, temporary/delegated powers, special use classes, maps, and encroachments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Zoning by-law drafting, direction, certification, and consultation

evidenceText: immediately proceed to draft a zoning by-law

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover the duty to draft and make a zoning by-law after a municipal plan, preparation direction, certification, and consultation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the timing, direction, certification, and consultation requirements for making or amending a zoning by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Zoning by-law zone standards, permits, services, unsafe structures, landscaping, and special uses

evidenceText: divide the municipality into zones

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 53(2) authorizes detailed zone standards, permit systems, service-arrangement restrictions, dangerous or unsightly building controls, landscaping standards, special use conditions, inclusionary zoning, and site unsuitability prohibitions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the main land, building, permit, service, appearance, special-use, inclusionary-zoning, and unsuitable-site controls a zoning by-law may contain.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Temporary authorizations, delegation, parking money, amendment fees, exemptions, and overlay zones

evidenceText: temporary period not exceeding one year

proposedGroups.reason: These provisions address temporary prohibited development authorizations, delegation and written delegation limits, payment in lieu of parking, amendment fees and procedures, development exemptions, and overlay zones.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a zoning by-law may handle temporary authorizations, delegated authority, parking payments, amendment applications, development exemptions, and overlay zones.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Use classes, integrated development zones, and protective terms for particular purposes

evidenceText: establish classes of purposes

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections authorize use classes, integrated development zones tied to section 59 proposals, and terms and conditions limited to property and public protection.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how zoning by-laws may classify uses, allow integrated development zones, and impose terms for particular purposes.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Zoning maps, affected streets, and good-faith encroachments

evidenceText: shall be shown on a map or plan

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require zone maps, allow maps to show affected streets and building lines, and define when small set-back or yard encroachments are not violations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how zoning maps form part of a by-law and when small set-back or yard encroachments are treated as good faith.

reason: Section 54 provides substantive validity and commencement conditions for a zoning by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Zoning by-law validity conditions and filing commencement

evidenceText: No zoning by-law is valid unless

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections identify certification, section 111 compliance, Ministerial filing compliance, and when the by-law comes into force.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the validity requirements for a zoning by-law and when it comes into force after filing.

reason: Section 55 has distinct variance authorities for advisory bodies and development officers plus rules preventing duplicate requests and allowing delegation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Advisory committee or regional service commission zoning variances

evidenceText: may permit

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 55(1) lets the advisory committee or regional service commission permit similar or compatible uses and reasonable variances subject to terms and conditions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the advisory committee or regional service commission may permit a proposed use or zoning by-law variance.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development officer zoning variances

evidenceText: A development officer may permit a reasonable variance

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 55(2) gives the development officer a narrower variance power for listed zoning requirements when desirable and consistent with the by-law and any plan.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which zoning variances a development officer may permit and the standard for granting them.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Same-variance request limits and development officer delegation

evidenceText: a request with respect to the same variance shall not be made

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections prevent the same variance request from being made to the other decision-maker after a determination and allow delegation of the development officer's variance power.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how section 55 prevents repeat variance requests and permits delegation by a development officer.

reason: Section 56 is a focused notice rule for requested zoning uses or variances.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Neighbour notice for proposed use or variance requests

evidenceText: may give notice to owners of land in the neighbourhood

proposedGroups.reason: The section authorizes notice to nearby owners and states the required description of land, requested use or variance, and representation right.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what notice may be given to neighbouring owners when a proposed use or zoning variance is requested.

reason: Section 57 states a narrow financial-use rule for money received in lieu of off-street parking.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Special account for off-street parking money

evidenceText: paid into a special account

proposedGroups.reason: The section requires money received under paragraph 53(2)(k) to be kept in a special account and used only for public off-street parking land.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how council must account for and spend money received instead of off-street parking.

reason: Section 58 is a short substantive condition for describing or showing an integrated development zone.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Integrated development zone compliance with proposal rules

evidenceText: An integrated development zone shall not be described or shown

proposedGroups.reason: The section ties the description or mapping of an integrated development zone to compliance with paragraph 53(3)(b).
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that an integrated development zone cannot be described or shown unless paragraph 53(3)(b) is complied with.

reason: Section 59 is a substantial re-zoning agreement source with separate topics for resolution contents, filing and binding effects, cancellation and reversion, and security.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Re-zoning resolutions, terms, time limits, and agreements

evidenceText: set out the proposal

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 59(1) lets council set out a proposal, impose terms and conditions, prescribe time limits, restrict development to the proposal, and enter into an agreement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what council may put in a re-zoning resolution or agreement for a specific proposal.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Filing, variation notice, and binding effect of re-zoning resolutions or agreements

evidenceText: shall not become effective until certified copies

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections state when resolutions and agreements become effective, how variations or new agreements are noticed and filed, and their binding effect on subsequent owners.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when re-zoning resolutions or agreements become effective, how they are varied, and how they bind later owners.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Cancellation, zone reversion, notice, and repeal steps for re-zoning agreements

evidenceText: the council may cancel the resolution or agreement

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections allow cancellation for contrary development or missed time limits, provide for zone reversion on filing, require notice and repeal steps, and preserve reversion despite notice or repeal failures.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what happens when a re-zoning resolution or agreement is cancelled and how the land reverts to its former zone.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Security before entering re-zoning agreements

evidenceText: may require a person to deliver a performance bond

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 59(9) allows council to require a performance bond, negotiable instrument, or other acceptable security before entering an agreement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what security council may require before entering a re-zoning agreement.
